title: Pasta alla Norcina
subtitle: Rigatoni with Italian sausage, cream, and a little nutmeg
excerpt: A rich Umbrian pasta of crumbled Italian sausage cooked with white wine, cream, and nutmeg. Simple to make and deeply satisfying on a cold night.
sourceNotes: Pasta alla Norcina originates from Norcia in Umbria, central Italy, traditionally made with local pork sausage.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sausage and cream sauce can be made up to 2 hours ahead. Reheat gently and add a splash of pasta water to loosen before tossing with fresh-cooked pasta.

content.text: Pasta alla Norcina is a creamy sausage pasta with just enough nutmeg to give it warmth. The sausage should be crumbled small so it coats every piece of pasta. Do not skip the splash of pasta water at the end as it binds the sauce.

items.prepNote: finely grated, plus more to serve

content.text: Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Add salt generously. Cook the rigatoni until just shy of al dente, about 1 minute less than the packet says.
While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the crumbled sausage. Fry for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks, until browned.
Push the sausage to one side. Add the garlic slices and fry for 1 minute.
Pour in the white wine. Let it bubble and reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Add the cream and nutmeg. Simmer gently for 3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Scoop out a mugful of pasta water before draining. Drain the pasta and add it to the sauce pan.
Toss over a medium heat for 2 minutes. Add a splash of pasta water to loosen the sauce if needed. Remove from the heat.
Stir in the parmesan and black pepper. Divide between bowls. Serve with more parmesan on the side.

items.cause: The heat was too high when the cream was simmering.
items.fix: Keep the cream at a gentle simmer, never a rolling boil. A splash of pasta water and gentle stirring will help bring it back.

items.symptom: The sausage is sitting in a pool of grease.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough, so the fat rendered without browning.
items.fix: Make sure the oil is hot before adding the sausage. Drain excess fat if needed before adding the wine.

items.cause: It was fully cooked before going into the sauce or was not tossed with enough liquid.
items.fix: Pull the pasta 1 minute early and finish it in the sauce. Add pasta water little by little until the consistency is glossy and loose.
